overall.summary: The functional scope matches the RFP well, but pricing and dates aren’t committed, and support terms and risks are missing.

client_priorities.title: Continuity over new technology
client_priorities.text: The RFP rules out a database migration and asks for rollout with minimal disruption. Proposals that change NordFrame’s infrastructure should lose points.
client_priorities.suggestion: Completeness vs. RFP set to High

citations.label: RFP, Req. 3
citations.quote: no migration to a new database

client_priorities.title: Decisions will rely on this data
client_priorities.text: The client asks for risks and limitations explicitly because stock decisions will be made from the dashboard.

citations.label: RFP, Req. 7
citations.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

client_priorities.title: Fixed budget and dates
client_priorities.text: A published budget that includes Year 1 support, and a pilot deadline. Deferred pricing or undated plans are a real gap here.
client_priorities.suggestion: Pricing and Timeline stay at Medium

citations.label: RFP, Budget
citations.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

citations.label: RFP, Timeline
citations.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

criteria.name: Completeness vs. RFP
criteria.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
criteria.comment: Requirements 1–4 are covered, 5 only partly, 6 and 7 not at all.

criteria.name: Risks & assumptions
criteria.description: Dependencies and risks are flagged, not hidden.
criteria.comment: No risks or assumptions, although both price and schedule depend on “discovery” and “integration complexity”.

criteria.name: Pricing clarity
criteria.description: Price stated, broken down, easy to follow.
criteria.comment: A €70,000–€110,000 range instead of a price. The low end is below the client’s range, and it’s unclear whether Year 1 support is included.

criteria.name: Timeline clarity
criteria.comment: Phases are named but have no dates. “Within the timeframe you’ve outlined” repeats the ask instead of committing to it.

citations.label: Proposal, Timeline
citations.quote: Exact scheduling will be confirmed once we begin discovery

criteria.name: Data accuracy & validation
criteria.description: Says how inventory figures are checked against reality before anyone relies on them.
criteria.comment: Phased onboarding is meant to reduce disruption, but nothing says how the dashboard figures are checked against the current stock records before a site goes live.

criteria.name: Problem understanding
criteria.description: Reflects the client’s actual stated problem and goals, not a generic pitch.
criteria.comment: Names the 6 warehouses and the spreadsheet plus legacy setup. Doesn’t pick up the “minimal disruption” goal.

citations.label: Proposal, Our Understanding
citations.quote: six warehouses currently rely on spreadsheets and a legacy system

criteria.name: Scope & deliverables
criteria.description: Deliverables are specific; clear what is and isn’t included.
criteria.comment: All four functional requirements are described specifically, including site-level roles and the no-migration constraint. Support and exclusions aren’t defined.

criteria.name: Legacy system & spreadsheets
criteria.description: Says what happens to the old legacy system and the spreadsheets after go-live.
criteria.comment: The spreadsheets and the legacy system are named in the understanding, but the proposal never says what happens to them after go-live.

requirements.name: Web dashboard for all 6 sites
requirements.ask: A web-based dashboard showing real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses.
requirements.finding: Real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses.

citations.label: Proposal, Proposed Solution
citations.quote: real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses

requirements.name: Automated low-stock alerts
requirements.ask: Alerts to warehouse managers when items fall below a configurable threshold.
requirements.finding: Per-item configurable thresholds, notifying warehouse managers automatically.

requirements.name: Existing PostgreSQL, no migration
requirements.ask: Integration with the existing PostgreSQL inventory database, with no migration to a new database.

rfp_citation.label: RFP, Req. 3
rfp_citation.quote: no migration to a new database

requirements.finding: Built on the existing PostgreSQL database; states no migration is required.

requirements.name: Role-based access
requirements.ask: Warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all sites.
requirements.finding: Managers limited to their own site; HQ sees all sites.

citations.label: Proposal, Proposed Solution
citations.quote: warehouse managers see only their own site's data

requirements.name: Onboarding plan for 6 sites
requirements.ask: A data migration / onboarding plan for all 6 sites with minimal disruption.
requirements.finding: Warehouses will be onboarded “in phases”, but not in what order, when, or how disruption is avoided.
requirements.suggested_fix: Turn the rollout bullet into a short plan: the pilot site and why, the order of the other 5 sites, and a parallel run with the existing spreadsheets before each cutover.

requirements.name: Support & maintenance terms
requirements.ask: Support and maintenance terms after go-live, including response times and SLAs.
requirements.finding: Support after go-live isn’t mentioned, nor whether the price covers the first year of support the budget includes.
requirements.suggested_fix: Add a “Support & maintenance” section: response times by severity, support hours, and confirmation that Year 1 support is included in the price.

requirements.name: Assumptions, limitations, risks
requirements.ask: Clear documentation of assumptions, limitations or risks, since inventory decisions will rely on the system.
requirements.finding: No risks or assumptions are documented.
requirements.suggested_fix: Add “Risks & assumptions”. The price depends on “integration complexity”, so name what drives it (schema quality, access rights) and what happens to cost and dates if discovery finds problems.

requirements.name: Within budget
requirements.ask: €80,000–€120,000 total, including the first year of support.

rfp_citation.label: RFP, Budget
rfp_citation.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

requirements.finding: A €70,000–€110,000 range with a firm quote after discovery. The low end is below the client’s range and Year 1 support isn’t stated as included.
requirements.suggested_fix: Give one estimated total inside €80,000–€120,000 with a line-item breakdown including Year 1 support, and state the maximum change after discovery (for example ±10%).

requirements.name: Pilot in 3 months, rollout in 6
requirements.ask: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months; all 6 sites within 6 months.

rfp_citation.label: RFP, Timeline
rfp_citation.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

requirements.finding: Discovery, pilot and rollout are named with no dates attached.
requirements.suggested_fix: Date each phase, for example: discovery Weeks 1–3, pilot live at one site by Week 12, all 6 sites by Week 24.

other_issues.label: Unsupported
other_issues.title: Credentials without evidence
other_issues.finding: “Several mid-size distribution companies” gives the client nothing to verify.
other_issues.suggested_fix: Name one comparable project, anonymised if needed: number of sites, database, time to go-live.
